newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open weaker.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open weaker.

text.p: COMEX copper was called to open weaker Monday as follow-through selling from Friday's slide pushed the market lower overnight.
July COMEX was called 0.40 to 0.50 cent below Friday's finish of 118.10 cents a lb.
Friday, July COMEX settled 4.05 cents lower in heavy volume after a downside test triggered sell stops.
On LME Monday, copper fell through a string of support levels on liquidation despite the cash to three months backwardation remaining strong at $132/$137, up slightly from Friday.
On ACCESS, July COMEX was down 1.05 cents at 117.05 cents a lb, traded 118.45 to 117.05 cents.
Monday, LME stocks rose 225 tonnes to 121,775 tonnes.
CFTC's Commitments of Traders report issued late Friday showed that the trade was still heavily short with the speculators long.
Commercials held 40,164 short positions and 7,555 long positions in week ended 17 June. Speculators held 21,075 long positions and 2,420 short positions.
COMEX stocks Friday rose 675 short tons to 49,630 short tons.
